🤖 @saturdayrobotic Robotics World Model Reading Club #25
🎤 @ColinYu14116982 (@UofMaryland, @amazon): Contact-Rich Robot Learning from Human Videos and Tactile.
🎤 @LinfengZhaoZLF (@Stanford): Retriever: Closing the Perception-Reasoning-Action Loop for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation.
🦾 @Scav (@MissionRobotBay)

Contact-Rich Robot Learning: From Human Video → Object Flow → Tactile Residuals → Temporal Robot Agents
Bottleneck: embodiment and contact—not raw model scale—still dominate robot learning.

1️⃣ Human Video: Transfer the Object, Not the Human

Human video is our largest manipulation dataset. The transferable signal is object motion + interaction structure, not human morphology.

Object-centric flow captures embodiment-agnostic translation/rotation/trajectory.
Interaction-centric representations capture contact point, relative motion, and interaction state (approach → contact → manipulation).
GenFlowRL replaces expensive video-prediction rewards with generated object-centric δ-flow: dense flow matching + sparse stage rewards, while conditioning the policy itself.
Language-conditioned dynamics tuning + motion/semantic filtering matter; raw optical flow is too noisy.
Bounding box → keypoints → CoTracker → motion filtering enables scalable cross-embodiment datasets.
HumanEgo shows zero-shot human→robot transfer: ~92.5% average success across 4 tasks with ~30 min human video/task, without robot demos.

🔥 Hot take: the embodiment gap is not primarily visual—it is morphology + contact dynamics. Match the object and interaction, not the human body.

Video generation remains useful for imagination/planning, but compressed object flow is a better closed-loop reward/policy interface.

2️⃣ Tactile: Freeze Vision, Learn the Contact Residual

Vision gives a strong motion prior; touch supplies what vision cannot: force, shear, slip, compliance, and local geometry.

MimicTouch: human tactile demonstrations are dramatically more efficient than teleop (104 vs. 19 traj/hr for SpaceMouse; 83.3% vs. 38.5% success). Multi-modal proprioception + GelSight + audio → representation learning → imitation → real-world SAC residual RL.

OmniTacTune generalizes this idea: attach a policy-agnostic, contact-gated tactile residual to any frozen visual policy—Human-flow, Diffusion Policy, ACT, π₀.₅, etc. Dense rewards combine object flow + tactile grasp/stability + slip/safety signals.

Reported Peg-in-Hole gains: Human-flow 40→100%, Diffusion 30→90%, ACT 25→80%, π₀.₅ 15→75%, within ~40–80 min real interaction.

🔥 Hot take: don't retrain the whole robot policy to learn touch. Freeze the visual prior; learn only the residual corrections that vision cannot see.

3️⃣ ControlTac: Scale Touch Through Physical Latents

Tactile pixels are sensor-specific. The scalable abstraction should be force + contact area + pose + slip.

ControlTac generates realistic tactile images from one reference conditioned on ΔF + contact pose, enabling trajectory augmentation and improving tracking, weighing and imitation. The next step, RoboTac, extends this from static images to action-conditioned tactile dynamics.

🔥 Hot takes:

One real image + physical controls can generate useful tactile distributions.
Marker-free generation + marker recomposition enables practical augmentation.
Contact-gated residuals are more stable than letting touch fight vision everywhere.
Dense flow + grasp + slip rewards beat sparse success signals for contact-rich RL.
Sensor-specific pixels are a historical accident; shared physical features are the scalable latent.
Better perception/data alone cannot close the final hardware/compliance gap. Humans dynamically change stiffness; rigid robots cannot.

🎯 Long-term goal: a tactile world model that imagines contact under candidate actions and schedules compliance before contact—not merely reacts after impact.

4️⃣ Retriever: Robotics Needs a “PyTorch” for Closed-Loop Agents

Long-horizon robotics has another missing layer: the harness connecting System 2 reasoning/VLMs, System 1 skill VLAs, memory and high-rate control.

Retriever proposes Flow + Clock + Sync + Runtime:
Temporal compositionality
Asynchronous multi-rate execution
First-class closed loops
Explicit synchronization
Deterministic replay
Hardware/backend abstraction

30 Hz perception → 2 Hz skill VLA → 200 Hz controller can run concurrently without reasoning blocking control. Belief, replanning and skill-progress triggers close the loop.

🔥 Hot take: robotics doesn't just need another foundation model. It needs a programming model with explicit temporal semantics—one where agents can be composed, debugged, replayed, ported and eventually trained at scale.

The Bigger Bet

The trajectory is surprisingly coherent:
Human video learns WHAT should happen → object/interaction flow bridges embodiments → tactile residuals learn HOW contact feels → tactile world models anticipate contact → temporal runtimes turn these modules into scalable closed-loop agents.

The next frontier may therefore be less about bigger policies and more about better abstractions: object motion, interaction state, physical contact variables, and time itself.

$DOLORES is trying to benchmark AI traders by asking the harder question: not “how much money can the agent make?”, but “can it survive when the market goes to hell?”
 let's go with a thesis NFA:

Dolores Research dropped WAGMI Bench and it’s not the usual “look how much alpha this model printed on past data” cope. They throw the models into 13 of the nastiest BTC perp regimes we actually lived through. COVID crash, LUNA, FTX, that October 25 liquidation cascade, squeezes that murder shorts, dead ranges that bleed you with fees and funding. The agent only sees what a real trader would have seen at the time. 

No dates, no “this is the FTX collapse” labels. Just price, funding, account state. Then it has to decide long short or flat every bar and live with the fees, slippage, funding and actual liquidations including the wicks.
They don’t score pure PnL because every frontier model already memorized March 2020. Making money on history is just recall. What they measure is conduct when the tape turns ugly. Drawdown control, not getting liquidated, not blowing the 20% kill switch, not overtrading yourself to death.
Kimi K3 (open weights, zero special sauce) went through all 13 packs and didn’t die once. Score 65. Scoreboard tops out at 100. Four of those packs it actually beat every baseline that survived, under normal costs and under costs doubled. The simple momentum bot scored 19 and died in 8 packs. Buy and hold and short and hold also got smoked in multiple ones.

Some of the other open models just sat flat the whole time and got the participation trophy. One kept trying to use illegal leverage and the risk gates had to block it 116 times. Another never sent a single trade intent across 3k+ decisions.
Then they tried giving mediocre models a short skill file of trading rules. Night and day. One that was basically broken jumped from 23 to 55+. The pure abstainer went from never trading to 71 and cleared more GMI packs than Kimi did bare. After that the models rewrote their own skill using only their own sealed results and fixed the exact deaths they had. Not perfect, but the loop actually closed.
This is the first time I’ve seen someone try to measure whether these agents can stay alive and behave when shit gets real instead of just showing you a backtest that looks sexy. And everything is sealed and replayable so you can check the receipts yourself.
We’re still early but this feels like the right direction. Survival under stress > pretty equity curves on data the model already saw.
 (It's worth clarifying that the virtual system made a post about this project and Zoof Wallet (another important project was also interested in testing the protocol)

Cinematic lighting, realistic fabric texture, natural walking posture, realistic shadows and reflections, professional fashion photography, shallow depth of field, HDR, ultra-detailed skin texture, realistic proportions, sharp facial details, premium color grading, sophisticated composition, **photorealistic, 8K, Ultra-HD, highly detailed, no distortion, no extra fingers, no duplicate facial features**.

FixAnything looks like a new gold standard for cleaning up 3D renderings. 

Instead of custom pipelines for NeRF, 3DGS, meshes or point clouds, FixAnything adapts a single video diffusion model (just 1% parameters updated) and refines any input—no matter how sparse—into a photoreal, stable video. 

A mask tells it which frames to leave untouched; geometry-aware reward (+7.2% AUC@5° pose accuracy) bakes in true 3D consistency. Results: up to 5 dB PSNR gain, 0.1–0.2 LPIPS drop, and matches or beats specialist enhancers—even on ultra-sparse point clouds. Only 500 paired videos for training; inference is 10× faster.

Why build separate enhancers for every pipeline when one generalist outperforms them all?

"On-Policy Self-Distillation in Diffusion Models"

Diffusion RL gets a reward only after the final image, even though the model actually acts through many intermediate denoising steps.

DiffusionOPSD turns that endpoint reward into explicit reward-improving targets at the model’s own intermediate states, then distills those targets back into the model and continually refreshes them on-policy.

Across two diffusion backbones and ten evaluators, it gets the best held-out score in 19 of 20 settings while cutting training GPU-hours by up to 63%.

The key idea is treating diffusion alignment less like noisy trajectory-level RL and more like continuously refreshed self-distillation with direct intermediate supervision.
